text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High eviction rate observed on kvcache for cluster-prod-3 — automated throttles triggered (eviction_rate=92% over 5m).

alice.ong: seeing this on our paging metrics dash. lat p50 bumped ~30ms but OOM risk flagged. jumping in.

benji: noticed a spike in attention-paged allocator faults around the same time. could be a workload change that warmed a lot of long-context requests.

carla: what jobs started around 11:30? Any large-batch rerank or long-chat jobs?

elena.prod: customer monitoring shows 3 customers with increased error 503s: acme-corp, neohealth, betaai. all in EU region on node pool gp4-prod-3.

alice.ong: thanks @elena.prod. marking P1 for customer impact. starting mitigation checklist.

benji: quick mitigation idea: reduce kvcache max pages per session to 32 and enable aggressive eviction for non-LRU hot keys. can push a config flag but it will increase token regen for very long contexts.

carla: can we flip runtime flag remote: attention_paging.enabled=false for gp4-prod-3? that disables paging path and will keep everything resident (higher risk) but stop trashing the paged allocator. only do if we have headroom.

dave.sre: cluster has ~12% headroom on GP memory across pool. safe to toggle for a short window.

alice.ong: plan: 1) reduce per-session kv pages to 32 (non-disruptive config update) 2) respin runtime on gp4-prod-3 with attention_paging disabled if eviction persists 3) run kv_compact script to free stale pages 4) watch customer errors. anyone object?

benji: +1. I'll prepare the config diff and a quick rollback.

carla: I can handle the respin. will do canary on a single AZ first.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: runtime-config-update on cluster-prod-3 by benji. CI checks passed. ETA 60s.

alice.ong: rolling the config now: applying ConfigMap change kv.max_pages_per_session=32 to prod-3.

benji: pushed. logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T11:47:12Z] apply config kv.max_pages_per_session=32 to cluster-prod-3
[2026-03-15T11:47:13Z] updated nodes: 6/6
[2026-03-15T11:47:14Z] metric: kvcache.eviction_rate -> 65% (was 92%)
```

carla: eviction dropped but still above baseline. kicking canary: disabling attention paging on one node group (gp4-prod-3-azb).

dave.sre: monitoring memory usage. if resident set > 85% on canary, abort.

carla: canary applied. canary logs: 
```
INFO runtime: attention_paging disabled
INFO allocator: using resident KV path
WARN migration: migrating live KV pages to resident arena
```

benji: canary looks stable. resident memory increased ~7% but no OOM. eviction on canary -> 4%.

alice.ong: rolling disable to remaining nodes in pool. doing 2 at a time. ETA ~10m.

elena.prod: customer error rates dropping: acme-corp 503->1.2% from 6.8%, neohealth 503->0.9% from 5.1%.

carla: all nodes rolled. eviction rate now 3-6% across pool. paging faults back to baseline.

benji: running kv_compact job now to shrink fragmented bitmaps. command: 
```
/k8s/prod/scripts/kv_compact --cluster prod-3 --pool gp4-prod-3 --safe-mode
```
deploy-bot: Job started: kv_compact (job-id: 202603151148_kvcomp).

alice.ong: while compaction runs, we should add safety knobs: lower default max_kv_pages globally and add alert to detect sudden warmup spikes.

dave.sre: filed ENGOPS ticket #INF-4422 to reduce default and add alert. linking to thread.

elena.prod: putting a short update for customer comms: affected customers saw transient 5xxs, mitigation applied (config and node respin), ongoing compaction, will follow up with RCA.

carla: quick note for handoff — if eviction rate creeps back above 50% after rollback, revert to previous config and open a deeper runtime debug. There may be a regression in paged allocator's free-list coalescing path.

benji: collecting allocator traces and CUDA error logs. attaching snippet: 
```
ERROR cuda: out-of-memory during page_migration (device=0)
TRACE allocator: free_list fragmentation: gaps=312, largest_block=3MB, requested=8MB
```

alice.ong: excellent. I'm taking the next 2 hours of on-call. leaving notes:
- Incident started 11:46 UTC (thread_ts 1922103333)
- Root cause hypothesis: sudden warmup of long-context requests causing attention-paging thrash + fragmentation -> eviction spike -> transient 503s
- Mitigations applied: reduced per-session kv pages, disabled attention paging on gp4-prod-3 pool, ran kv_compact, monitoring
- Customer impact: acme-corp, neohealth, betaai saw transient errors; now reduced
- Follow-ups: ENGOPS #INF-4422, ENG-RUNTIME to investigate free-list coalescing and add better compaction heuristics

dave.sre: noted. handing off to alice. I'll be available if needed. :thumbsup:

elena.prod: adding a short post-incident note to support channel and drafting customer notification.

benji: I'll keep digging into allocator codepaths and prepare a patch to improve migration atomics. posting findings in eng-runtime channel later.

carla: leaving a small runbook update in docs: how to toggle attention_paging per-pool and safe memory thresholds.

alice.ong: thanks everyone. keeping thread open while kv_compact finishes. if no regressions in 2h I'll mark as mitigated and start RCA timeline.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. severity downgraded to SEV3.
